# Vocab Diet: Reshaping the Vocabulary of LLMs via Vector Arithmetic

> Vocab Diet builds compositional vocabularies for language models: instead of a separate token for every word form (walk, walked, walking, Walk), words are composed from a shared base word and transformation vectors (walked = walk + past tense), at both input and output. Paper by Yuval Reif, Guy Kaplan and Roy Schwartz (The Hebrew University of Jerusalem), Findings of ACL 2026.

## Key results

- The GPT-4 tokenizer has 24.6k English whole-word tokens; ignoring case leaves 17.7k, and grouping inflections and derivations leaves 14.3k base words (42% fewer). The same bases and transformations can compose 98k further English words.
- LLMs interpret composed embeddings (base + transformation vector) as the intended word, especially for inflections and capitalization, including many out-of-vocabulary words (Patchscopes, Llama-3.1-8B; also Arabic, German, Russian, Spanish). Derivations mostly fail.
- Existing models can be adapted to a compositional vocabulary with a frozen backbone (transformation vectors plus LoRA on the last 8 layers) removes ~10k tokens from Llama-3.1-8B and OLMo-2-7B and 7.8k from Qwen2.5-7B; English downstream average 66.9 → 65.9 for Llama-3.1-8B; decoding 0.8% slower.
- Reallocating the 10k freed slots to Arabic, Russian, German and Spanish (2.5k each) improves bytes per token by 9.3% on average at the same vocabulary size.
- Pretraining 124M models from scratch with a compositional vocabulary needs ~42% fewer vocabulary entries. English: the same words as GPT-2's BPE vocabulary with 41.6% fewer entries, so tokenization is unchanged (bits per byte 1.08 vs 1.09). Spanish: 41.8% fewer entries plus composed out-of-vocabulary words, improving compression from 4.77 to 4.92 bytes per token at higher bits per byte (1.00 vs 1.11).
- Across 13 models, morphology is encoded less linearly in embeddings as English vocabulary size grows.

- Related: [CoBPE](https://co-bpe.github.io/) (COLM 2026), which attaches articles, prepositions and punctuation to base tokens.
